name: tui-template
tagline: A working skeleton for a new tui-tools tool
description:
The starting point for a new tool in the family. Press **Use this template**, rename it, replace one package, and you have a tool that looks and behaves like the rest.

It is not a pile of TODOs: it is a working tool. It lists the files in a directory and can update a file's timestamp, which is deliberately trivial — what matters is the shape around it, and that shape is already correct: the action table that generates the key map, the help screen and the confirm dialog; the backend interface with a real and a fake implementation; `--demo`; CI; and GoReleaser.

This `tool.json` is itself the example. It is a valid manifest, validated against [the schema](https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-kit/blob/main/schema/tool.schema.json) on every CI run, and the values are the ones you replace.

screenshots.caption: The list: the four bands every tool in the family draws
The confirm dialog, showing the exact command line before it runs
The help screen, generated from the action table

notes.impact: `touch -h` is missing, so the timestamp of a symlink is set on its target instead of on the link

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-template
cd tui-template && make demo
source.note: Or press "Use this template" on GitHub, which is the point of it.

pacman.note: The template is never packaged. This entry shows your tool's shape.

apt.note: The template is never packaged. This entry shows your tool's shape.

dnf.note: The template is never packaged. This entry shows your tool's shape.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-template/releases/download/v{version}/tui-template_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-template
sudo install -m0755 tui-template /usr/local/bin/tui-template
binary.note: The template is never released. Your tool is, once you tag v0.1.0.

security.needs_sudo: Only the touch action escalates, and only when the configured prefix is non-empty. Listing a directory is an ordinary read. Replace this sentence with what your own tool escalates for.
